---
title: "Step 2 — Install the packages and run the check"
subtitle: "Step 2 of 5"
---

**Time:** 20 minutes, mostly waiting.
**Before you start:** [Step 1](install.qmd) finished, and RStudio open.
**When you finish:** 15 packages installed, and a pass or fail report you send
us in Step 3.

You do not need to download or save any files. Both scripts run straight from
the course website.

## Step 1 of 3 — Install the 15 packages

1. Open RStudio.
2. Click once inside the **Console** pane, at the bottom left.
3. Copy the code box below. Paste it into the Console. Press **Enter**.

```r
source("https://drarunmitra.github.io/iisc-epi-shortcourse/setup/install_packages.R")
```

4. Leave the computer alone until it finishes.

**You should see:** lines of text scrolling past, naming each package as it
installs. This takes 10 to 25 minutes the first time, and longer on a slow
connection. You are finished when the `>` prompt comes back and stops moving.

**If it does not work:** if R asks
`Do you want to install from sources the package which needs compilation?`,
type `n` and press **Enter**.

::: {.callout-warning}
## Do not interrupt it
If you close RStudio part way through, some packages are left half-installed.
The script installs only what is still missing, so it is safe to run again. Run
it again and let it finish.

Red text in R is not always an error. Most of it is ordinary progress output
that R prints on the error stream.
:::

## Step 2 of 3 — Run the check

1. Click once inside the **Console** pane.
2. Copy the code box below. Paste it into the Console. Press **Enter**.

```r
source("https://drarunmitra.github.io/iisc-epi-shortcourse/setup/check_setup.R")
```

**You should see:** about 10 lines, each starting with a tick (✔), an
exclamation mark (!) or a cross (✖), then this last line:

```
You are ready for 21 September. See you at IISc.
```

**If it does not work:** read the line that starts with a cross. It names the
fix. Then read [Troubleshooting](../resources/troubleshooting.qmd).

| Symbol | Means |
|---|---|
| ✔ | that check passed |
| ! | a warning; usually fine, read the text |
| ✖ | that check failed; fix this one |

## Step 3 of 3 — Copy the output

1. Select the whole output of the check in the Console.
2. Copy it.

**You should see:** the text on your clipboard, ready to paste into an email.

**If it does not work:** if the output has scrolled away, run the check line
again.

::: {.callout-note}
## Why this matters
R on its own does very little. The work is done by packages: bundles of
functions other people wrote. This course uses 15 of them.

The check does not ask only whether a package is installed. It tests 9
behaviours: that R is 4.1.0 or newer; that the native pipe `|>` runs; that
RStudio can report its version; that Quarto is installed **and** the `quarto` R
package can see it; that all 15 packages are present; that the core packages
load rather than only sit on disk; that `epitools` returns the right risk
ratio from a known table; that your working folder is writable; and that a tiny
Quarto document renders from end to end.

The last one is the important one. It is the only test that proves R, Quarto and
your packages work together rather than side by side.

Send us a failing report too. A failure we see on Wednesday is a working laptop
by Friday. A failure we first see on Monday morning is a lost session.
:::
